OSHI is not just a messenger — it\'s a communication protocol for digital freedom. Built on principles of sovereignty, privacy, and resilience.
It works without servers, using peer-to-peer mesh networking to route messages through direct Bluetooth/Wi-Fi connections or multi-hop relay nodes.
Every message is protected by the Signal Double Ratchet cryptosystem, ensuring perfect forward secrecy and post-compromise security — even across offline relays and out-of-order delivery.
Zero metadata, zero tracking, zero compromise. Your conversations belong only to you.
No central authority, no single point of failure. Power distributed across the network.
You control your identity, your data, and your connections.
Works in low-connectivity and offline scenarios. Communication keeps flowing.
Strong end-to-end encryption with forward secrecy on every message.
Messages relay through trusted peers to reach their destination, even offline.
Encrypted IPFS storage ensures delivery when direct mesh isn\'t available.
Advanced message buffering handles network chaos gracefully.
Send photos and videos with AES-256-GCM encryption, decrypted only by recipient.

OSHI is a secure, decentralized messaging app that uses mesh networking and end-to-end encryption to protect your privacy.
OSHI uses Bluetooth and WiFi to create a peer-to-peer network with nearby devices. Messages hop between devices until they reach the recipient.
Yes! OSHI uses the Double Ratchet algorithm (same as Signal) for end-to-end encryption. Only you and your recipient can read messages.
What if I lose my device?
Make sure to backup your keys in Settings > Backup Keys. Without your backup, you cannot recover your identity.
Can I use OSHI without internet?
Yes! OSHI\'s mesh networking allows you to send messages to nearby users without internet.
Go to New Message and either scan your contact\'s QR code, share your QR code, or paste their public key.
OSHI is built on trust and respect. Please follow these guidelines:
This app has not undergone a professional security audit. While we use strong encryption, use at your own discretion.
OSHI does not require an account, a phone number, or an email. Your identity stays on your device.
Without internet, messages hop from phone to phone — about 100 m directly, and further when other people nearby relay them along. A paired Meshtastic LoRa radio reaches about 30 km.
Designed for scenarios when a country is disconnected from the internet. Communicate freely even when networks are down.
This is beta software. Features may change and bugs may occur.
For security, messages and calls are only received when the app is open. In crisis situations, if your phone is locked, notifications only arrive after the app is open for 2+ seconds.
When contacts are not nearby, messages are stored encrypted on IPFS (decentralized storage) and voice calls use our relay server. All data remains end-to-end encrypted.
OSHI is a collaborative encrypted messenger. Messages can travel up to 10km through nearby devices — even without internet! Let\'s show you around.

No phone number, no account — just a code
Tap the + button, then "My code". That QR code IS your address in OSHI. There is no phone number and no username.
Sitting together? Have them tap "Scan" and point their camera at your code. You are connected — that is the whole step.
Far apart? Tap "Invite by link" and send that link however you like — SMS, email, any app. Opening it on a phone with OSHI adds you.
No internet at all? Open "Nearby". Any phone running OSHI within about 100 m appears there over Bluetooth, and you can add each other with no network.
Cashu ecash — OSHI never holds your money
OSHI has no wallet and never holds your money. It carries a Cashu token — ecash backed by bitcoin — the way it carries a photo.
You need a Cashu wallet first. eNuts, Minibits, or cashu.me in a browser: all free, about a minute to set up.
In the wallet, choose a mint and add a little money over Lightning. A few hundred sats is plenty to try this.
Make a token: tap Send in the wallet, enter an amount, copy. You get a long line of text starting with cashuB. That text IS the money.
They tap Redeem and the money lands in their wallet. A token sent to you looks the same: tap Redeem. OSHI is only the envelope.
In the chat, type / in the message box and choose /pay, then paste the token. OSHI shows the amount before it sends, so you can check it.

A Cashu token is cash. Anyone who gets the text can spend it, and whoever redeems it first keeps it — so send it only to the person you mean. OSHI cannot ask the mint whether a token has already been spent: it is yours only once your own wallet redeems it.
